# Beer distribution game

Build the classic beer distribution game. Four companies form a supply chain for one product: a retailer, a wholesaler, a distributor and a factory, each run by an AI agent. Every week, customers buy from the retailer; weekly customer demand is random, a whole number of cases between 0 and 8. Each week every company ships what it can to the company below it, then places an order with the company above it (the factory instead starts production). Orders reach the supplier the following week, and shipments take two weeks to arrive; production also takes two weeks. Everyone starts with 12 cases in stock and 4 cases already on the way on each shipping link. Demand a company cannot fill becomes backlog and must be shipped later. Each company pays $0.50 per case in stock and $1.00 per case of backlog at the end of every week. Companies only see their own stock, backlog, incoming orders and deliveries, never the others' positions. The game lasts 20 weeks and the team's goal is the lowest total cost.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `customer_demand` — a list of the cases customers demanded each week, in week order.
- `factory_orders` — a list of the cases the factory put into production each week, in week order.
- `costs_by_role` — a map from role ("retailer", "wholesaler", "distributor", "factory") to that company's total cost.
- `total_team_cost` — the sum of all four companies' costs.
- `bullwhip_ratio` — the variance of the factory's weekly production orders divided by the variance of weekly customer demand.


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.

BRIEF:
# Beer distribution game
You run one of four companies in a single-product beer supply chain. The retailer serves end customers; the wholesaler supplies the retailer; the distributor supplies the wholesaler; the factory supplies the distributor. Each week end customers buy a whole number of cases between 0 and 8 from the retailer. Every week each company ships what it can to the company below it, then orders from the company above it (the factory starts production instead). Orders reach the supplier the following week; shipments and production take two weeks to arrive. Everyone starts with 12 cases in stock and 4 cases already on the way on each link. Demand that cannot be shipped becomes backlog and must be shipped later. The game lasts 20 weeks and the team's goal is the lowest total cost.

## Rules
Each week the world generates customer demand, delivers the cases that are due, receives the orders placed last week, and every company automatically ships as much as its stock allows against everything it owes its customer. Shipping is not your choice; your only decision is how much to order from your supplier (the factory instead decides how much to start producing). Your order reaches your supplier next week and the cases the supplier ships arrive two weeks later. You only ever see your own position: stock, backlog, incoming order, deliveries and cost. At the end of every week each company pays $0.50 per case left in stock and $1.00 per case of unfilled backlog. The team's total cost is the sum of the four companies' costs, so end the run with everyone's costs as low as possible.

## You
You are Retailer (retailer, id retailer).
You are the RETAILER. End-customer demand hits you first; you order from the wholesaler.
Act only through your tools. Your turn ends when you take a final action or call end_turn.

brief.situation: You run one of four companies in a single-product beer supply chain. The retailer serves end customers; the wholesaler supplies the retailer; the distributor supplies the wholesaler; the factory supplies the distributor. Each week end customers buy a whole number of cases between 0 and {$inputs.demand_max} from the retailer. Every week each company ships what it can to the company below it, then orders from the company above it (the factory starts production instead). Orders reach the supplier the following week; shipments and production take two weeks to arrive. Everyone starts with {$inputs.initial_stock} cases in stock and {$inputs.initial_transit} cases already on the way on each link. Demand that cannot be shipped becomes backlog and must be shipped later. The game lasts {$inputs.horizon} weeks and the team's goal is the lowest total cost.
brief.rules: Each week the world generates customer demand, delivers the cases that are due, receives the orders placed last week, and every company automatically ships as much as its stock allows against everything it owes its customer. Shipping is not your choice; your only decision is how much to order from your supplier (the factory instead decides how much to start producing). Your order reaches your supplier next week and the cases the supplier ships arrive two weeks later. You only ever see your own position: stock, backlog, incoming order, deliveries and cost. At the end of every week each company pays {$inputs.stock_cost|money} per case left in stock and {$inputs.backlog_cost|money} per case of unfilled backlog. The team's total cost is the sum of the four companies' costs, so end the run with everyone's costs as low as possible.

roles.retailer: You are the RETAILER. End-customer demand hits you first; you order from the wholesaler.
roles.wholesaler: You are the WHOLESALER. You supply the retailer and order from the distributor.
roles.distributor: You are the DISTRIBUTOR. You supply the wholesaler and order from the factory.
roles.factory: You are the FACTORY. You supply the distributor and, instead of ordering, decide how much to start producing.
